get.summary: Get the brand icon for a sender domain
get.description: Tries the domain's BIMI SVG, then Google's and DuckDuckGo's favicon services; a subdomain without an icon falls back to its registrable domain. Results are cached server-side (hits 7 days, misses 24 hours). A domain that is not a plausible hostname (empty, longer than 253, or containing anything but ASCII letters, digits, `.` and `-`) gets 204, never 4xx.

200.description: Icon bytes. Content-Type is the upstream's when it starts with `image/` (commonly image/svg+xml, image/png, image/x-icon, image/vnd.microsoft.icon, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp), otherwise image/png. At most 256 KiB. Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800

204.description: No icon for this domain, or the domain is invalid; empty body. Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400

get.summary: List outbound jobs that are queued, waiting to retry, in flight, or failed for good
get.description: Up to 100 job ids from each of the pending list, the retry set and the in-flight list, de-duplicated, one row per job whose record still exists; then the 100 newest jobs that failed for good, newest first. Each row is the job's stored envelope with `message_data_b64` removed and `status` overwritten with the list it was found in. Envelope fields are whatever the writer stored, so extra fields (e.g. `last_attempt_at`) can appear. A failed row is the failure record instead: `id`, `status: "failed"`, `sender` and `recipient` (empty when the record predates them and the job is gone), `last_error` (the reason) and `failed_at`.

last_attempt_at.description: Set by the sender after an attempt

failed_at.description: Failed rows only: when the job failed for good, unix seconds

get.description: CalDAV (RFC 4791) and CardDAV (RFC 6352). One handler serves every method on /dav and below, including PROPFIND and REPORT, which OpenAPI cannot name; only GET, PUT and DELETE are listed. Layout: /dav/ and /dav/principals/{user}/ (principal), /dav/calendars/{user}/ (calendar home), /dav/calendars/{user}/{calendar}/ (calendar: `default` holds the user's events, and each subscribed feed is a read-only calendar named after it), /dav/calendars/{user}/{calendar}/{uid}.ics (event), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/ (address-book home), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/default/ (the address book), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/default/{uid}.vcf (card). The {user} segment must be the authenticated user, else 403. Events are the rows the calendar conflicts check reads; a card's addresses are offered by /api/contacts. PUT honours If-Match and If-None-Match: *, answers 201 on create and 204 on update with an ETag, 400 for a body that does not parse, 412 on a failed precondition, 403 for a feed calendar, and 5xx when the store fails.

200.description: iCalendar or vCard text, with an ETag header

403.description: The path names another user, or a read-only calendar

delete.description: CalDAV (RFC 4791) and CardDAV (RFC 6352). One handler serves every method on /dav and below, including PROPFIND and REPORT, which OpenAPI cannot name; only GET, PUT and DELETE are listed. Layout: /dav/ and /dav/principals/{user}/ (principal), /dav/calendars/{user}/ (calendar home), /dav/calendars/{user}/{calendar}/ (calendar: `default` holds the user's events, and each subscribed feed is a read-only calendar named after it), /dav/calendars/{user}/{calendar}/{uid}.ics (event), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/ (address-book home), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/default/ (the address book), /dav/addressbooks/{user}/default/{uid}.vcf (card). The {user} segment must be the authenticated user, else 403. Events are the rows the calendar conflicts check reads; a card's addresses are offered by /api/contacts. PUT honours If-Match and If-None-Match: *, answers 201 on create and 204 on update with an ETag, 400 for a body that does not parse, 412 on a failed precondition, 403 for a feed calendar, and 5xx when the store fails.

403.description: The path names another user, or a read-only calendar

get.description: PROPFIND answers 207 with the calendar-home-set (/dav/calendars/{user}/) and addressbook-home-set (/dav/addressbooks/{user}/). OPTIONS answers 200 with Allow and DAV headers.

bearerAuth.description: Session token from /api/auth/login or API key (mlrs_...)

status.description: `healthy` when a kevy ping succeeds, otherwise `degraded`

uptime_secs.description: Seconds since this webapi process started

kevy.description: Result of a kevy ping made by this request

pg.description: Always null: this lane has no PostgreSQL backend

token.description: Session token, the same value as the mailrs_session cookie. Apps send it as Authorization: Bearer; the web client relies on the HttpOnly cookie.

is_admin.description: Whether the account may use the admin console. The one server-side rule (super user, or any admin.* permission); the client shows or hides admin entries by it.
Whether the account may use the admin console. The one server-side rule (super user, or any admin.* permission); the client shows or hides admin entries by it.

invite_method.description: iTIP method of the message's text/calendar part, upper-case (REQUEST / REPLY / CANCEL / PUBLISH / COUNTER). Empty for mail that carries no calendar part, which is nearly all of it. Computed at ingest and carried on every message read, so a list can mark an invitation without fetching one.

invite_payload.description: The typed invitation, present only when invite_method is set. Fields follow RFC 5545 (uid, sequence, summary, location, organizer, attendees, dtstart, dtend, rrule, recurrence_id, status), plus dtstart_utc / dtend_utc: the instants resolved on the server against the invitation's own VTIMEZONE. Clients must prefer those — a zoned wall-clock plus a Windows zone name such as "Pacific Standard Time" is not a moment a browser can evaluate.

rsvp_status.description: The answer this reader already gave: ACCEPTED / TENTATIVE / DECLINED, or null.

rsvp_at.description: Unix seconds, as a string, of when that answer was recorded.

undo_seconds.description: Hold an immediate send this many seconds (capped at 30) so DELETE /api/mail/pending/{message_id} can still stop it. Ignored when scheduled_at is set.

reactions.description: Map of message ID to reaction summaries

value.description: domain (example.com) / email (user@example.com) / cidr (10.0.0.0/8 or 2001:db8::/32). CIDR must be canonical (host bits zero).

key.description: Full key if recently created, null otherwise

url.description: Webhook endpoint URL (must be https, or http for localhost)

signing_secret.description: HMAC signing secret (save immediately, cannot be retrieved again)

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; read from `occurred_at` or `timestamp` in the stored row, always serialized as `timestamp`

client_ip.description: Address of the person signing in to the calling service; the login guard counts it instead of the caller.
Address of the person signing in to the calling service; the login guard counts it instead of the caller.

occurrence.description: RFC 5545 RECURRENCE-ID instant for per-occurrence RSVP

status.description: HTTP status the sender's endpoint returned

message.description: Transport error, when the request never completed

address.description: an example address; any tag works

codes.description: one-time codes found near words such as code / verification

address.description: Email address; must contain `@` after trimming

DavMultistatus.description: WebDAV multistatus XML document (RFC 4918 section 13), served as application/xml; charset=utf-8 with a `DAV: 1, 2, calendar-access, addressbook` header
